title: Qualify bounded IR graphs, matrices and correct expanded DAG frontier
commitMessage: feat: qualify bounded immutable mathematical IR graphs and matrices

contribution.summary: Observe four independent typed IR boundary REDs, harden all public application/restriction factories to enforce depth and expanded node quotas, add rectangular immutable homogeneous matrices and domain-correct assumptions, then qualify nine adversarial tests and all locked Math/package regressions to close M2-W01-C02.
contribution.value: Makes the new provider-neutral .NET IR safely bounded on whole immutable graph representations rather than only local factory arity, while rejecting accidental numeric widening and assumption leakage across symbol domains.
debtChanges: A matrix shape may admit up to 4096 cells, but whole-graph evaluation applies the stricter 1024 expanded-node ceiling; tests prove that 1023 matrix cells plus the matrix node are admitted.

The IR carries stable bound/free symbol identities but does not implement executable binder evaluation, alpha-equivalent substitution, or full unbound-variable validation. These remain explicit future capabilities.
Canonical JSON, semantic hashes, provider execution and OpenMath/Content MathML adapters remain out of scope until subsequent M2 chunks; no external AURA adoption is claimed.

Retry 0 was a pre-attempt failure: the expanded DAG GREEN oracle treated 1023 admitted nodes as >1024. Retry 1 fixes both RED/GREEN to test 2047 rejected nodes, and makes evidence updates idempotent on DWF target re-entry.
contribution.nextAction: Prepare M2-W01-C03 versioned canonical JSON codec with independent RED for lossless rationals, quantities, symbol binding and exclusions; reject unknown versions and malformed graphs without guessing semantic equivalence.

achievements.achievement: Four independently executed prechange REDs show unchecked total graph depth, shared-DAG expanded node budget, absent matrix type and domain-leaking assumptions.
Public IR factories enforce 1024 expanded node occurrences and depth 32, homogeneous immutable matrix shape, defensive copying, domain-aware assumptions and duplicate-guard rejection.

All four REDs turn green; nine adversarial tests check exact admission/rejection boundaries, shared subgraphs, matrix shapes, immutable data, distinct symbol domains, scopes and nonfinite policies, plus full IR/quantity/foundation regressions and package inspection.

IR adversarial boundaries and immutable collection integration are qualified, including explicit distinct 4096-cell local matrix shape and stricter global 1024-node budget, with future binder/codec limitations recorded.

The admitted immutable typed IR chunk is qualified through exact/approximate scalars, real-domain restrictions, stable symbol identity, public whole-graph quotas and homogeneous matrices; canonical JSON remains the next independent chunk.
